subject: Terra Nexus — VPC ops handoff and control/data plane clarifications
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@terranexus.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Lucia Romano <lucia@terranexus.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Terra Nexus — VPC ops handoff and control/data plane clarifications

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. We're preparing the ops handoff for our on‑prem private deploy (Terra Nexus datacenter A) and need a concise set of artifacts so our network team can complete firewall rules and the change window. Can you confirm the following and share any evidence artifacts you have: 

- Control plane placement: do you expect Redwood control plane to live in Redwood cloud with private endpoints to our VPC, or do we run a customer‑hosted control plane component inside our VPC?
- Egress and NAT: recommended pattern for model outbound calls (metrics, telemetry, model updates) — NAT vs. private link vs. proxy. Which ports/proto need egress?
- KMS and keying: if we use our KMS, what endpoints/certificates do we need configured?
- Audit logs & retention: format and sample evidence (CloudTrail/packet logs) we can ingest into our SIEM.
- Operational cutover checklist: minimal port list, test plan, rollback cues.

We have an internal change window next sprint (Dec 15–18). If we can get the diagram and a short MAP (mutual action plan) before Dec 8 that would be great.

I'll loop in the ops alias below: ops@terranexus.com.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
VP Engineering, Terra Nexus
samir@terranexus.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@terranexus.com>
Cc: Lucia Romano <lucia@terranexus.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Terra Nexus — VPC ops handoff and control/data plane clarifications

Hi Samir — thanks, and appreciate the timeline. Attaching a concise packet to get ops started: terra‑nexus‑vpc‑diagram‑v1.pdf (annotated control/data plane), and ops‑evidence‑checklist.csv (format we typically provide for SOC/ops teams). High level answers inline below so your network team has context quickly.

— Control plane placement
Our recommended default is Redwood managed control plane (hosted) with private, mTLS authenticated API endpoints to your VPC via a customer‑owned ingress (PrivateLink / VPC peering pattern depending on cloud/provider). This keeps orchestration and model versioning in our control plane while runtime/model traffic (data plane) stays under your control.

If you require an air‑gapped or on‑prem control plane we can provide a customer‑hosted control component; that option increases operational surface (patching, HA) — see attachment controlplane‑placement‑proposal.md for details.

— Egress and NAT
Preferred pattern for your setup: keep data plane in your VPC, allow egress for telemetry to our metrics ingestion endpoints over TLS (443) through a controlled NAT or egress proxy. Model downloads/updates should be pulled from our signed artifact service (HTTPS 443) and validated. For telemetry/health checks we recommend outbound to specific FQDNs only; see ops‑evidence‑checklist.csv for FQDNs and IP ranges.

— KMS
We support external KMS (customer‑managed) over standard TLS endpoints. You will need to whitelist the KMS API endpoints and ensure IAM roles/service accounts are provisioned. We document certificates and signing CA requirements in the attachment.

— Audit logs & retention
We produce audit logs (activity, API calls, and request metadata) in JSON that can be exported to your SIEM. The CSV has example fields and retention guidance. If you need syslog/CEF forwarding, our ops agent can be configured to push to your collector via TLS.

— Cutover checklist (minimal)
1) Open outbound 443 to listed FQDNs (metrics, artifacts).
2) Allow inbound TLS for private endpoint IPs if using PrivateLink.
3) ACL: allow TCP 22 for the maintenance window only (if you opt for host‑level support).
4) Smoke tests: token generation, health ping, short generate request, and embedding call.
5) Rollback: revert routing to previous NAT and flush cache.

I've proposed a short MAP inside the PDF and added comments where we need your ops team to confirm IP ranges. Can Karthik and Jonas jump in with any control‑plane runbook items?

— Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: terra‑nexus‑vpc‑diagram‑v1.pdf, ops‑evidence‑checklist.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@terranexus.com>, Lucia Romano <lucia@terranexus.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2027 11:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Terra Nexus — VPC ops handoff and control/data plane clarifications

Thanks Tessa — quick engineering clarifications from our side (see controlplane‑placement‑proposal.md attached):

1) HA and control plane heartbeat: if you go with Redwood hosted control plane, we operate cross‑region control plane instances. For on‑prem deployments where the control component runs in your VPC we recommend a 3‑node controller set with keepalived for failover and a health probe path (/_hc). Health probes use mutual TLS to our monitoring collector; implement ACLs to the collector IPs.

2) Data path separation: runtime inference (gRPC/TCP) stays in your private subnets. We suggest a small egress proxy (envoy) in a dedicated subnet so you can centrally manage TLS termination and outbound filtering. This also simplifies key management if you bring your own KMS.

3) Ports: minimal set we tested in staging: 443 (outbound HTTPS for artifacts/telemetry), 853 (optional DNS over TLS), 8143 (internal gRPC for model fetches) — 8143 only if you deploy model cache services in edge pods. Our attachment lists these with explanations.

4) Observability hooks: please enable outbound to our metrics ingestion endpoint and provide a sample log file so we can validate the schema before cutover.

Action items we need from Terra Nexus ops:
- Confirm whether you prefer PrivateLink (VPC endpoint) or NAT egress model.
- Provide the maintenance window (single or rolling) and confirm whether 22 will be permitted during that window.

I'll coordinate the runbook updates once we have your preference.

—Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: controlplane‑placement‑proposal.md

From: Samir Patel <samir@terranexus.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Lucia Romano <lucia@terranexus.com>, ops@terranexus.com
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2027 09:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Terra Nexus — VPC ops handoff and control/data plane clarifications

Tessa / Karthik — this is helpful, thank you. A couple quick items from ops after reviewing the attachments: 

- We prefer PrivateLink for the control plane endpoints (reduces routing changes on our side).
- Maintenance window: Dec 16, 02:00–06:00 UTC for the initial cutover (rolling for edge pods).
- We'll allow outbound 443 to the FQDN list and will stand up an envoy egress proxy per Karthik's suggestion.
- We need a short MAP with owners and a rollback trigger list (if 3rd party latency > 150ms for 10m, revert). Can you produce a 1‑page MAP and share DocuSign SOW link for the onboarding line items?

If you can send the 1‑page MAP and the SOW link today we can lock the window.

Thanks — looping ops alias.
Samir
VP Engineering, Terra Nexus
